For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

# kitty

Keeps track of shared trip costs and works out who owes whom. Needs only the
`python3` that comes with macOS. Run it from this folder:

    python3 -m kitty init EUR
    python3 -m kitty member add Alice
    python3 -m kitty member add Bob
    python3 -m kitty rate set USD 0.92
    python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 45 Dinner --currency USD --category food
    python3 -m kitty balances
    python3 -m kitty settle

Everything is saved in `kitty.json` in the folder you run it from. Add
`--help` to any command to see its options, e.g. `python3 -m kitty expense add --help`.

## Notes for scripts

- Reports (`member list`, `expense list`, `payment list`, `balances`, `settle`,
  `history`, `report`) print one line of JSON. Money is a string with two decimals, in the
  main currency except an expense's or payment's own `amount`.
- `expense add` prints just the new expense ID. Other commands that change
  data print a short human-readable confirmation.
  `payment add` includes the payment ID in its confirmation, for use with
  `payment remove ID`.
- Errors go to stderr and exit with status 1.
- Amounts may have at most two decimals and use a dot (`12.50`, not `12,50`).
- When an amount doesn't split evenly, the spare cents go to the people with
  the biggest fractional share (ties go to whoever joined the group first), so
  shares always add up exactly to the total.
- A foreign-currency expense or payment is converted with the rate set at the
  time it's recorded. Changing the rate later doesn't change old entries.
- Categories are stored in lowercase, so `Food` and `food` are the same.
- A member who appears in any expense or payment can't be removed. Remove those
  entries first.

Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

"""Command-line interface and logic for kitty.

All data lives in ./kitty.json. Money is handled with Decimal and kept to
whole cents; when an amount is split, leftover cents are handed out so the
shares always add up exactly to the expense total.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import datetime
import json
import os
import re
import sys
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

DATA_FILE = "kitty.json"
CENT = Decimal("0.01")

MONEY_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$")
NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+(\.\d+)?$")
CURRENCY_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z]{3}$")


class KittyError(Exception):
    """A problem caused by the user's input or data; shown as a plain message."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsing and formatting helpers


def fmt(value):
    return str(Decimal(value).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def parse_money(text, what="amount"):
    text = text.strip()
    if not MONEY_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(
            f"{what} must be a number with at most two decimals, like 12.50 (got {text!r})"
        )
    value = Decimal(text)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be greater than zero (got {text!r})")
    return value


def parse_number(text, what):
    text = text.strip()
    if not NUMBER_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be a number, like 2 or 0.92 (got {text!r})")
    value = Decimal(text)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be greater than zero (got {text!r})")
    return value


def parse_currency(text):
    text = text.strip()
    if not CURRENCY_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(f"currency must be a three-letter code like EUR or USD (got {text!r})")
    return text.upper()


def parse_date(text):
    if text is None:
        return datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    try:
        return datetime.date.fromisoformat(text.strip()).isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"date must look like 2026-07-14 (got {text!r})")


def parse_id(text, what):
    if not text.strip().isdigit():
        raise KittyError(f"{what} ID must be a whole number (got {text!r})")
    return int(text)


def validate_name(text):
    name = text.strip()
    if not name:
        raise KittyError("name cannot be empty")
    if "," in name or "=" in name:
        raise KittyError(f"name cannot contain ',' or '=' (got {text!r})")
    if name.startswith("-"):
        raise KittyError(f"name cannot start with '-' (got {text!r})")
    return name


def output(data):
    print(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Storage


def new_kitty(base):
    return {
        "version": 1,
        "base": base,
        "members": [],
        "rates": {},
        "next_expense_id": 1,
        "next_payment_id": 1,
        "next_seq": 1,
        "expenses": [],
        "payments": [],
    }


def load():
    if not os.path.exists(DATA_FILE):
        raise KittyError(f"no {DATA_FILE} in this folder; start one with: python3 -m kitty init EUR")
    try:
        with open(DATA_FILE, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        raise KittyError(f"could not read {DATA_FILE}: {e}")
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("version") != 1:
        raise KittyError(f"{DATA_FILE} is not a kitty file this version understands")
    return data


def save(data):
    tmp = DATA_FILE + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
        f.write("\n")
    os.replace(tmp, DATA_FILE)


def take_seq(data):
    seq = data["next_seq"]
    data["next_seq"] += 1
    return seq


def require_member(data, name):
    if name not in data["members"]:
        known = ", ".join(data["members"]) or "nobody yet"
        raise KittyError(f"{name!r} is not in the group (members: {known})")
    return name


def rate_for(data, currency):
    if currency == data["base"]:
        return Decimal(1)
    if currency not in data["rates"]:
        raise KittyError(
            f"no exchange rate for {currency}; set one first with: "
            f"python3 -m kitty rate set {currency} RATE"
        )
    return Decimal(data["rates"][currency])


def to_base(amount, rate):
    base = (amount * rate).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    if base <= 0:
        raise KittyError("amount is too small to record once converted to the main currency")
    return base


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Splitting


def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split `total` (whole cents) in proportion to `weights` (ordered list of
    (name, weight)). Leftover cents go to the largest remainders, ties broken
    by list order, so the result always sums to `total` exactly."""
    cents = int(total / CENT)
    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    floors = []
    for i, (name, w) in enumerate(weights):
        exact = Decimal(cents) * w / weight_sum
        whole = int(exact)  # exact is non-negative, so int() floors
        floors.append([name, whole, exact - whole, i])
    leftover = cents - sum(f[1] for f in floors)
    for f in sorted(floors, key=lambda f: (-f[2], f[3]))[:leftover]:
        f[1] += 1
    return {name: Decimal(whole) * CENT for name, whole, _, _ in floors}


def parse_pairs(data, text, option, parse_value):
    pairs = []
    seen = set()
    for item in text.split(","):
        if "=" not in item:
            raise KittyError(f"{option} expects NAME=VALUE pairs separated by commas (got {item!r})")
        name, value = item.split("=", 1)
        name = require_member(data, name.strip())
        if name in seen:
            raise KittyError(f"{name} appears twice in {option}")
        seen.add(name)
        pairs.append((name, parse_value(value, f"{option} value for {name}")))
    return pairs


def parse_names(data, text, option):
    names = []
    for item in text.split(","):
        name = require_member(data, item.strip())
        if name in names:
            raise KittyError(f"{name} appears twice in {option}")
        names.append(name)
    return names


def split_weights(data, args, amount):

    if args.among is not None:

"""Command-line interface and logic for kitty.

All data lives in ./kitty.json. Money is handled with Decimal and kept to
whole cents; when an amount is split, leftover cents are handed out so the
shares always add up exactly to the expense total.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import datetime
import json
import os
import re
import sys
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

DATA_FILE = "kitty.json"
CENT = Decimal("0.01")

MONEY_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$")
NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+(\.\d+)?$")
CURRENCY_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z]{3}$")


class KittyError(Exception):
    """A problem caused by the user's input or data; shown as a plain message."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsing and formatting helpers


def fmt(value):
    return str(Decimal(value).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def parse_money(text, what="amount"):
    text = text.strip()
    if not MONEY_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(
            f"{what} must be a number with at most two decimals, like 12.50 (got {text!r})"
        )
    value = Decimal(text)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be greater than zero (got {text!r})")
    return value


def parse_number(text, what):
    text = text.strip()
    if not NUMBER_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be a number, like 2 or 0.92 (got {text!r})")
    value = Decimal(text)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be greater than zero (got {text!r})")
    return value


def parse_currency(text):
    text = text.strip()
    if not CURRENCY_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(f"currency must be a three-letter code like EUR or USD (got {text!r})")
    return text.upper()


def parse_date(text):
    if text is None:
        return datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    try:
        return datetime.date.fromisoformat(text.strip()).isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"date must look like 2026-07-14 (got {text!r})")


def parse_id(text, what):
    if not text.strip().isdigit():
        raise KittyError(f"{what} ID must be a whole number (got {text!r})")
    return int(text)


def validate_name(text):
    name = text.strip()
    if not name:
        raise KittyError("name cannot be empty")
    if "," in name or "=" in name:
        raise KittyError(f"name cannot contain ',' or '=' (got {text!r})")
    if name.startswith("-"):
        raise KittyError(f"name cannot start with '-' (got {text!r})")
    return name


def output(data):
    print(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Storage


def new_kitty(base):
    return {
        "version": 1,
        "base": base,
        "members": [],
        "rates": {},
        "next_expense_id": 1,
        "next_payment_id": 1,
        "next_seq": 1,
        "expenses": [],
        "payments": [],
    }


def load():
    if not os.path.exists(DATA_FILE):
        raise KittyError(f"no {DATA_FILE} in this folder; start one with: python3 -m kitty init EUR")
    try:
        with open(DATA_FILE, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        raise KittyError(f"could not read {DATA_FILE}: {e}")
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("version") != 1:
        raise KittyError(f"{DATA_FILE} is not a kitty file this version understands")
    return data


def save(data):
    tmp = DATA_FILE + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
        f.write("\n")
    os.replace(tmp, DATA_FILE)


def take_seq(data):
    seq = data["next_seq"]
    data["next_seq"] += 1
    return seq


def require_member(data, name):
    if name not in data["members"]:
        known = ", ".join(data["members"]) or "nobody yet"
        raise KittyError(f"{name!r} is not in the group (members: {known})")
    return name


def rate_for(data, currency):
    if currency == data["base"]:
        return Decimal(1)
    if currency not in data["rates"]:
        raise KittyError(
            f"no exchange rate for {currency}; set one first with: "
            f"python3 -m kitty rate set {currency} RATE"
        )
    return Decimal(data["rates"][currency])


def to_base(amount, rate):
    base = (amount * rate).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    if base <= 0:
        raise KittyError("amount is too small to record once converted to the main currency")
    return base


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Splitting


def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split `total` (whole cents) in proportion to `weights` (ordered list of
    (name, weight)). Leftover cents go to the largest remainders, ties broken
    by list order, so the result always sums to `total` exactly."""
    cents = int(total / CENT)
    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    floors = []
    for i, (name, w) in enumerate(weights):
        exact = Decimal(cents) * w / weight_sum
        whole = int(exact)  # exact is non-negative, so int() floors
        floors.append([name, whole, exact - whole, i])
    leftover = cents - sum(f[1] for f in floors)
    for f in sorted(floors, key=lambda f: (-f[2], f[3]))[:leftover]:
        f[1] += 1
    return {name: Decimal(whole) * CENT for name, whole, _, _ in floors}


def parse_pairs(data, text, option, parse_value):
    pairs = []
    seen = set()
    for item in text.split(","):
        if "=" not in item:
            raise KittyError(f"{option} expects NAME=VALUE pairs separated by commas (got {item!r})")
        name, value = item.split("=", 1)
        name = require_member(data, name.strip())
        if name in seen:
            raise KittyError(f"{name} appears twice in {option}")
        seen.add(name)
        pairs.append((name, parse_value(value, f"{option} value for {name}")))
    return pairs


def parse_names(data, text, option):
    names = []
    for item in text.split(","):
        name = require_member(data, item.strip())
        if name in names:
            raise KittyError(f"{name} appears twice in {option}")
        names.append(name)
    return names


def split_weights(data, args, amount):
    """Turn the split options into an ordered list of (name, weight)."""
    if args.among is not None:
        return [(n, Decimal(1)) for n in parse_names(data, args.among, "--among")]
    if args.exact is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(data, args.exact, "--exact", parse_money)
        total = sum(v for _, v in pairs)
        if total != amount:
            raise KittyError(f"--exact amounts add up to {fmt(total)} but the expense is {fmt(amount)}")
        return pairs
    if args.shares is not None:
        return parse_pairs(data, args.shares, "--shares", parse_number)
    if args.percent is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(data, args.percent, "--percent", parse_number)
        total = sum(v for _, v in pairs)
        if total != 100:
            raise KittyError(f"--percent values add up to {total} but must add up to 100")
        return pairs
    if not data["members"]:
        raise KittyError("the group has no members yet; add some with: python3 -m kitty member add NAME")
    return [(n, Decimal(1)) for n in data["members"]]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculations


def events(data):
    """All expenses and payments in date order (then the order they were added)."""
    items = [("expense", e) for e in data["expenses"]] + [("payment", p) for p in data["payments"]]
    return sorted(items, key=lambda item: (item[1]["date"], item[1]["seq"]))


def changes(kind, record):
    """How one expense or payment moves each person's balance."""
    delta = {}
    if kind == "expense":
        delta[record["payer"]] = Decimal(record["base_amount"])
        for name, share in record["shares"].items():
            delta[name] = delta.get(name, Decimal(0)) - Decimal(share)
    else:
        amount = Decimal(record["base_amount"])
        delta[record["from"]] = amount
        delta[record["to"]] = -amount
    return delta


def compute_balances(data):
    balances = {name: Decimal(0) for name in data["members"]}
    for kind, record in events(data):
        for name, change in changes(kind, record).items():
            balances[name] = balances.get(name, Decimal(0)) + change
    return balances


def compute_settlement(data):
    order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(data["members"])}
    balances = compute_balances(data)
    creditors = [[n, b] for n, b in balances.items() if b > 0]
    debtors = [[n, -b] for n, b in balances.items() if b < 0]
    transfers = []
    while creditors and debtors:
        creditors.sort(key=lambda c: (-c[1], order.get(c[0], 0)))
        debtors.sort(key=lambda d: (-d[1], order.get(d[0], 0)))
        creditor, debtor = creditors[0], debtors[0]
        amount = min(creditor[1], debtor[1])
        transfers.append({"from": debtor[0], "to": creditor[0], "amount": fmt(amount)})
        creditor[1] -= amount
        debtor[1] -= amount
        creditors = [c for c in creditors if c[1] > 0]
        debtors = [d for d in debtors if d[1] > 0]
    return transfers


def sorted_expenses(data):
    return sorted(data["expenses"], key=lambda e: (e["date"], e["seq"]))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Commands


def cmd_init(args):
    if os.path.exists(DATA_FILE):
        raise KittyError(f"a kitty already exists in this folder ({DATA_FILE}); delete or move it to start over")
    base = parse_currency(args.currency)
    save(new_kitty(base))
    print(f"Started a new kitty with {base} as the main currency.")


def cmd_member_add(args):
    data = load()
    name = validate_name(args.name)
    if name in data["members"]:
        raise KittyError(f"{name} is already in the group")
    data["members"].append(name)
    save(data)
    print(f"Added {name}.")


def cmd_member_remove(args):
    data = load()
    name = require_member(data, args.name)
    for kind, record in events(data):
        if name in changes(kind, record):
            raise KittyError(
                f"{name} is part of recorded expenses or payments, so they can't be removed; "
                "remove those first"
            )
    data["members"].remove(name)
    save(data)
    print(f"Removed {name}.")


def cmd_member_list(args):
    output(load()["members"])


def cmd_expense_add(args):
    data = load()
    payer = require_member(data, args.payer)
    amount = parse_money(args.amount)
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["base"]
    rate = rate_for(data, currency)
    description = " ".join(args.description).strip()
    if not description:
        raise KittyError("description cannot be empty")
    category = (args.category or "other").strip().lower()
    if not category:
        raise KittyError("category cannot be empty")
    date = parse_date(args.date)
    weights = split_weights(data, args, amount)
    base_amount = to_base(amount, rate)
    shares = allocate(base_amount, weights)

    expense_id = data["next_expense_id"]
    data["next_expense_id"] += 1
    data["expenses"].append({
        "id": expense_id,
        "seq": take_seq(data),
        "date": date,
        "payer": payer,
        "description": description,
        "amount": fmt(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": str(rate),
        "base_amount": fmt(base_amount),
        "category": category,
        "shares": {name: fmt(shares[name]) for name in data["members"] if name in shares},
    })
    save(data)
    print(expense_id)


def expense_view(e):
    keys = ["id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "base_amount", "category", "shares"]
    return {k: e[k] for k in keys}


def cmd_expense_list(args):
    data = load()
    output([expense_view(e) for e in sorted_expenses(data)])


def cmd_expense_remove(args):
    data = load()
    expense_id = parse_id(args.id, "expense")
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        if e["id"] == expense_id:
            data["expenses"].remove(e)
            save(data)
            print(f"Removed expense {expense_id} ({e['description']}).")
            return
    raise KittyError(f"there is no expense with ID {expense_id}")


def cmd_payment_add(args):
    data = load()
    sender = require_member(data, args.sender)
    receiver = require_member(data, args.receiver)
    if sender == receiver:
        raise KittyError("a payment needs two different people")
    amount = parse_money(args.amount)
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["base"]
    rate = rate_for(data, currency)
    date = parse_date(args.date)

    payment_id = data["next_payment_id"]
    data["next_payment_id"] += 1
    data["payments"].append({
        "id": payment_id,
        "seq": take_seq(data),
        "date": date,
        "from": sender,
        "to": receiver,
        "amount": fmt(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": str(rate),
        "base_amount": fmt(to_base(amount, rate)),
    })
    save(data)
    print(f"Recorded payment {payment_id}: {fmt(amount)} {currency} from {sender} to {receiver}.")


def payment_view(p):
    keys = ["id", "date", "from", "to", "amount", "currency", "base_amount"]
    return {k: p[k] for k in keys}


def cmd_payment_list(args):
    data = load()
    payments = sorted(data["payments"], key=lambda p: (p["date"], p["seq"]))
    output([payment_view(p) for p in payments])


def cmd_payment_remove(args):
    data = load()
    payment_id = parse_id(args.id, "payment")
    for p in data["payments"]:
        if p["id"] == payment_id:
            data["payments"].remove(p)
            save(data)
            print(f"Removed payment {payment_id} ({p['from']} to {p['to']}).")
            return
    raise KittyError(f"there is no payment with ID {payment_id}")


def cmd_rate_set(args):
    data = load()
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency)
    if currency == data["base"]:
        raise KittyError(f"{currency} is the main currency; its rate is always 1")
    rate = parse_number(args.rate, "rate")
    data["rates"][currency] = str(rate)
    save(data)
    print(f"1 {currency} = {rate} {data['base']}.")


def cmd_balances(args):
    output({name: fmt(b) for name, b in compute_balances(load()).items()})


def cmd_settle(args):
    output(compute_settlement(load()))


def cmd_history(args):
    data = load()
    name = require_member(data, args.name)
    running = Decimal(0)
    rows = []
    for kind, record in events(data):
        delta = changes(kind, record)
        if name not in delta:
            continue
        running += delta[name]
        if kind == "expense":
            description = record["description"]
        elif record["from"] == name:
            description = f"Payment to {record['to']}"
        else:
            description = f"Payment from {record['from']}"
        rows.append({
            "date": record["date"],
            "description": description,
            "change": fmt(delta[name]),
            "balance": fmt(running),
        })
    output(rows)


def cmd_report(args):
    data = load()
    totals = {}
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        category = totals.setdefault(e["category"], {})
        for name, share in e["shares"].items():
            category[name] = category.get(name, Decimal(0)) + Decimal(share)
    report = {}
    for category in sorted(totals):
        people = totals[category]
        report[category] = {n: fmt(people[n]) for n in data["members"] if n in people}
    output(report)


def cmd_export(args):
    data = load()
    columns = ["id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "category", "base_amount"]
    try:
        with open(args.file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            writer = csv.writer(f)
            writer.writerow(columns)
            for e in sorted_expenses(data):
                writer.writerow([e[c] for c in columns])
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"could not write {args.file}: {e.strerror}")
    print(f"Saved {len(data['expenses'])} expenses to {args.file}.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Argument parsing


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    """ArgumentParser that exits with status 1 (not 2) on bad usage."""

    def error(self, message):
        self.print_usage(sys.stderr)
        self.exit(1, f"{self.prog}: error: {message}\n")


def build_parser():
    parser = Parser(prog="kitty", description="Track shared trip costs and who owes whom.")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND")
    commands.required = True

    p = commands.add_parser("init", help="start a new kitty")
    p.add_argument("currency", help="main currency, e.g. EUR")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_init)

    member = commands.add_parser("member", help="manage the group").add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION")
    member.required = True
    p = member.add_parser("add", help="add a person")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_add)
    p = member.add_parser("remove", help="remove a person")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_remove)
    p = member.add_parser("list", help="list the group")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_list)

    expense = commands.add_parser("expense", help="manage expenses").add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION")
    expense.required = True
    p = expense.add_parser("add", help="record an expense")
    p.add_argument("payer")
    p.add_argument("amount")
    p.add_argument("description", nargs="+")
    split = p.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    split.add_argument("--among", metavar="A,B", help="split equally between only these people")
    split.add_argument("--exact", metavar="A=30,B=20", help="split by exact amounts")
    split.add_argument("--shares", metavar="A=2,B=1", help="split by shares")
    split.add_argument("--percent", metavar="A=60,B=40", help="split by percentages")
    p.add_argument("--currency", help="currency it was paid in (default: main currency)")
    p.add_argument("--date", help="YYYY-MM-DD (default: today)")
    p.add_argument("--category", help='category (default: "other")')
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_add)
    p = expense.add_parser("list", help="list expenses")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_list)
    p = expense.add_parser("remove", help="remove an expense")
    p.add_argument("id")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_remove)

    payment = commands.add_parser("payment", help="manage repayments").add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION")
    payment.required = True
    p = payment.add_parser("add", help="record that someone paid someone back")
    p.add_argument("sender", metavar="FROM")
    p.add_argument("receiver", metavar="TO")
    p.add_argument("amount")
    p.add_argument("--currency", help="currency it was paid in (default: main currency)")
    p.add_argument("--date", help="YYYY-MM-DD (default: today)")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_payment_add)
    p = payment.add_parser("list", help="list payments")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_payment_list)
    p = payment.add_parser("remove", help="remove a payment")
    p.add_argument("id")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_payment_remove)

    rate = commands.add_parser("rate", help="exchange rates").add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION")
    rate.required = True
    p = rate.add_parser("set", help="set what one unit of a currency is worth in the main currency")
    p.add_argument("currency")
    p.add_argument("rate")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_rate_set)

    p = commands.add_parser("balances", help="show who is up or down")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_balances)
    p = commands.add_parser("settle", help="suggest payments to even out")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_settle)
    p = commands.add_parser("history", help="everything that affected one person")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_history)
    p = commands.add_parser("report", help="each person's share of spending per category")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_report)
    p = commands.add_parser("export", help="save expenses to a CSV file")
    p.add_argument("file")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_export)
    return parser


def main(argv=None):
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        args.func(args)
    except KittyError as e:
        print(f"kitty: error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except OSError as e:
        print(f"kitty: error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0

"""Kitty: track shared trip costs and work out who owes whom."""

import contextlib
import csv
import io
import json
import os
import tempfile
import unittest

from kitty.cli import main


class KittyTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._old_cwd = os.getcwd()
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
        os.chdir(self._tmp.name)

    def tearDown(self):
        os.chdir(self._old_cwd)
        self._tmp.cleanup()

    def run_kitty(self, *argv, expect=0):
        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
            try:
                status = main(list(argv))
            except SystemExit as e:
                status = e.code
        self.assertEqual(status, expect, f"{argv}: stdout={out.getvalue()!r} stderr={err.getvalue()!r}")
        return out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

    def json(self, *argv):
        return json.loads(self.run_kitty(*argv)[0])

    def group(self, *names, base="EUR"):
        self.run_kitty("init", base)
        for name in names:
            self.run_kitty("member", "add", name)

    def test_sams_example(self):
        self.group("Alice", "Bob")
        self.run_kitty("rate", "set", "USD", "0.92")
        out, _ = self.run_kitty("expense", "add", "Alice", "45", "Dinner",
                                "--currency", "USD", "--date", "2026-07-14", "--category", "food")
        self.assertEqual(out.strip(), "1")
        self.assertEqual(self.json("expense", "list"), [{
            "id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner",
            "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food",
            "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"},
        }])
        self.assertEqual(self.json("balances"), {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"})
        self.assertEqual(self.json("settle"), [{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}])
        self.assertEqual(self.json("history", "Bob"), [
            {"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"},
        ])
        self.assertEqual(self.json("report"), {"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}})

    def test_member_list_and_remove(self):
        self.group("Alice", "Bob", "Carol")
        self.run_kitty("member", "remove", "Bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.json("member", "list"), ["Alice", "Carol"])

    def test_cannot_remove_member_with_activity(self):
        self.group("Alice", "Bob")
        self.run_kitty("expense", "add", "Alice", "10", "Taxi")
        self.run_kitty("member", "remove", "Bob", expect=1)
        self.run_kitty("expense", "remove", "1")
        self.run_kitty("member", "remove", "Bob")

    def test_equal_split_hands_out_leftover_cents(self):
        self.group("Alice", "Bob", "Carol")

I've added both features: `expense edit ID` and `--in CUR` on `balances` and `settle`. The 19 existing tests still pass unchanged, and with 7 new ones all 26 pass. The code is in `kitty/cli.py`, and I added short notes on both to the README.

**`expense edit ID`**
- It changes only the options you give. The ID stays the same, and so does the expense's place among others on the same date.
- If the amount or currency changes without a split option, it's split equally among the same people as before. That applies even when it was originally split by `--shares` or `--percent`.
- A split option works as it does in `add`. `--exact` must add up to the new amount, or to the current amount if you don't give `--amount`.
- A new currency is converted at its current rate. If only the amount changes, the expense keeps the rate it was recorded with, in line with "changing the rate later doesn't change old entries."
- Changing only the payer, description, date or category leaves the split alone.
- If any part of an edit is invalid, the whole edit is rejected and nothing is saved.

**`--in CUR`**
- Amounts are divided by the current rate and rounded to the cent. Using the base currency gives exactly the usual output, and a currency with no rate is an error.
- `settle` works out the transfers in the base currency first, then converts each one.

A few things behave in ways you might not expect:
- **Repeating the current value counts as no change.** For example, `--currency USD` on an expense that's already in USD doesn't re-split it or switch it to today's rate.
- **`expense edit 1` with no options is an error** ("nothing to change"). I wasn't sure whether you'd rather it quietly do nothing.
- **Rounding:** converted balances may not add up to exactly zero. A settle transfer too small to show in the chosen currency (it rounds to 0.00) is left out rather than shown as "0.00".
